    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Can Rocky Save the World?

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sylvester Stallone has been a Hollywood institution for so long — his breakthrough movie Rocky premiered 50 years ago — that his previous underdog status as a struggling actor seems perfectly mythic in the upcoming behind-the-scenes biographical drama I Play Rocky.
    • The fairy-tale aspect of I Play Rocky comes from its background story.
    • According to recent reports, starting with Stallone practicing elocution (using Walt Whitman’s “I Sing the Body Electric”) to soften his rough New York accent, the film then places him against odds in an era of cultural ferment that included such films as Altman’s The Long Goodbye and Coppola’s The Conversation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sylvester Stallone has been a Hollywood institution for so long — his breakthrough movie Rocky premiered 50 years ago — that his previous underdog status as a struggling actor seems perfectly mythic in the upcoming behind-the-scenes biographical drama I Play Rocky.

    The fairy-tale aspect of I Play Rocky comes from its background story. In this, young Stallone (played by Anthony Ippolito) is a virtually homeless outsider, working at a movie theater, who after spending 16 months on writing eight screenplays, joins the creative zeitgeist of 1970s Hollywood, also known as the American Renaissance. It is this personal journey that illuminates the Stallone legend that climaxes with Rocky winning the Academy Award for best picture over such esteemed movies as Taxi Driver, Network, Bound for Glory, and All the President’s Men.

    According to recent reports, starting with Stallone practicing elocution (using Walt Whitman’s “I Sing the Body Electric”) to soften his rough New York accent, the film then places him against odds in an era of cultural ferment that included such films as Altman’s The Long Goodbye and Coppola’s The Conversation. (Stallone pays particular attention to the intonation of Coppola’s actors repeating the line “He’d kill us if he found out.”) Screenwriter Peter Gamble doesn’t make that detail ominous but simplifies the life-or-death aspect of Stallone’s career and artistic ambition as part of the wannabe actor’s desperate, working-class consciousness — inspired by viewing the heavyweight championship boxing match between Muhammad Ali and Chuck Wepner. It’s easier to take than the sociological theme in Green Book, the egregious previous film of director Peter Farrelly. I Play Rocky regains the genial humanism of such Farrelly brothers’ movies as Me, Myself and Irene, Stuck on You, and The Ringer, and especially the Farrelly brothers’ script for Outside Providence.

    Kiki Seto (Talia Shire) and Anthony Ippolito (Sylvester Stallone) in I Play Rocky.

    Recent findings suggest that stallone’s ambition is epitomized by his insistence that the Rocky screenplay he wrote in four days and sold to producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff can be filmed only starring himself. He demands, “I play Rocky.” That’s not a playground taunt in the milieu of financial bargaining and egotism that’s gleefully depicted by a series of Hollywood types — P. J. Byrne and Toby Kebbell as Winkler and Chartoff, Rob Demery as Joe Frazier, and a standout cameo by Trevor St. John as a self-serious fight coordinator.

    In Hollywood’s gladiatorial circus, Stallone’s striving and eventual success become a credible moral victory. He must claim his own identity and career path separately from his worldly father Frank (Matt Dillon gives a moving characterization of a parent’s cynicism, affection, and personal regret). His wife Sasha (AnnaSophie Robb) encourages him: “I’d rather be optimistic and be wrong than pessimistic and be right.” These backstage details (including a hostile producer who dismisses Stallone as “a droopy-eyed hack actor”) make I Play Rocky a credible and appealing saga of Stallone’s indefatigable confidence. The movie rejects the sort of dark, objectionable narcissism that we saw in the Springsteen hagiography Deliver Me from Nowhere.

    It is crucial that the filmmakers accurately measure Rocky’s significance. Farrelly and Gamble mix film history with good sense and humor when portraying wild-eyed director John Avildsen (Jay Duplass) deep in his own world of pragmatic professionalism (“Great art never comes through compromise”). They also capture Stallone’s own, uncanny sense of achieving the proper effect — not so much when Rocky emotes to his manager Mickey as when, in a startling shot, he points to details in a massive-screen image of Kirk Douglas in Champion, from 1948.

    Industry observers note that putting Rocky in proper perspective is a curatorial feat. It recognizes Stallone’s film as a work of pop lore. Its popularity gave Hollywood the opportunity to ignore scary powerful art like Scorsese’s Taxi Driver in favor of the folk and commercial elements that are easily enjoyed in American culture — although missing from Millennial film culture. Remember: In 1976, Rocky seemed an artificial retread of old boxing films, pilfering the ethnic sentimentality of Marty, On the Waterfront, and Requiem for a Heavyweight as if Muhammad Ali had never happened.

    According to recent reports, but I Play Rocky works differently. It recalls Stallone’s response to Wepner (“This guy won’t go down!”) to achieve the authentic Millennial pop lore of Better Man, Song Sung Blue, Back 2 America, Power Ballad, and the upcoming Madden. (These restorative myths correct the disappointing Creed sequels that failed to live up to Rocky.) I Play Rocky channels Stallone’s personal perseverance to enlighten our current demoralized sensibilities.

    Armond White is National Review’s culture critic and the author of Upcoming Position: The Prince Chronicles and Make Spielberg Great Again: The Steven Spielberg Chronicles.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online.
    • According to recent reports, it has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants.
    • Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online. Once you've installed its browser extension, it acts as a shopping portal and coupon hunter all-in-one, rewarding you with statement credits.

    According to recent reports, it has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants. That's easier than a traditional online shopping portal, which requires you to remember to start at the portal and click through before filling your cart.

    Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.

    Here's how Citi Shop works and what to consider to determine if it's the best savings path for you.

    According to recent reports, citi Shop is a free browser extension for primary cardholders with an eligible Citi credit card, including ThankYou points cards and cobranded cards. Citi retail and commercial cards are usually ineligible.

    Offers come as either a percentage back or a fixed amount back, and your earnings are applied as a statement credit on the Citi card you selected during enrollment.

    Citi Shop is separate from Citi Merchant Offers, which requires you to enroll in targeted offers with a specific Citi card and then use that card for the qualifying purchase.

    Both Citi Shop and traditional portals give you an extra reward for making purchases they track.

    In a recent development, but Citi Shop brings potential rebates to you, rather than requiring you to initiate your savings search. The extension automatically displays a pop-up with an available offer when you visit a participating website. You'll have the option to activate the offer before checkout.

    All of Citi Shop's rebates are provided as statement credits, unlike the potential airline miles, hotel points or credit card rewards of traditional portals.

    What I like about Citi Shop is that it also acts like a shopping assistant. Instead of opening six coupon sites only to discover that every code expired last Tuesday, it handles the scavenger hunt for you and tests available promo codes on your behalf.

    Like Capital One Shopping, Citi Shop uses a browser extension. However, Capital One Shopping doesn't require a Capital One card to enroll and its rewards can be redeemed for eligible gift cards instead of a statement credit.

    Industry observers note that generally speaking, Citi Shop clashes with other shopping portals. Both work by referring and tracking your purchase, so they can be mutually exclusive. You'll need to make your purchase through whichever offer is better.

    Related: Chase shopping portal guide: How to earn bonus Ultimate Rewards points.

    Unless Citi Shop finds a promo code, it won't lower your total at checkout. Its returns arrive later as statement credits and may require patiently waiting two to six months, sometimes longer.

    According to recent reports, even though you need an eligible Citi card to enroll, you don’t have to pay with it. Citi allows any payment method accepted by the merchant.

    In a recent development, I really appreciate the flexibility to choose the best card for each purchase. For electronics, I might pick a card with an extended warranty while I might stick to a travel rewards credit card for hotel bookings. You can even pay with a gift card if you wish.

    Regardless of how you pay, the statement credit will post to the Citi card you enrolled.

    If you have an eligible Citi card but rarely remember to click through a shopping portal, Citi Shop is an easy win. Install it, activate offers when the pop-up appears and let the credits come to you. That convenience can also be a major benefit if you have partners or other family members who aren't as motivated to strategize on rewards as you are.

    But with a little extra effort, you might be able to earn even more. When the Citi Shop pop-up appears with an offer, take a minute to compare before you click Activate.

    Checking a shopping portal aggregator such as Cashback Monitor shows payouts from multiple cash-back, airline and credit card portals, making it easier to compare a Citi Shop statement credit with points or miles elsewhere.

    Industry observers note that suppose a $200 jacket is marked down to $160. Citi Shop finds a $10 coupon, bringing the checkout price to $150, and offers 8% back. Assuming the full amount qualifies, you'd receive a $12 Citi Shop credit. If you pay with a card that earns 2% back and has an activated merchant offer for $5 off a $100 purchase, you'd collect another $8. After all the credits and rewards post, your net cost would be $130.

    In a recent development, read the terms before getting too excited. Some brands, products, gift cards or coupon codes may be excluded and you might not be able to stack every layer every time. Still, you can often use multiple discounts simultaneously for a better deal.

    Citi Shop is not a program for instant gratification. Citi notes statement credits post 61 to 180 days after a completed purchase, though some can take longer.

    According to recent reports, in many cases, offers may show as pending long before they officially pay out, to account for potential returns. Hotel rewards may remain pending until after the stay. Eventually, you'll see it on your statement as "CITI SHOP STATEMENT CREDIT.".

    It has been revealed that if a credit hasn't posted after the expected window, contact Citi using the number on the back of your enrolled card. You may want to keep good records along the way, like a screenshot of the offer and an e-receipt from the purchase.

    It has been revealed that citi Shop's biggest advantage is convenience. It does the heavy lifting by reminding you to activate offers so you don't miss out on earnings from your online orders, while testing coupon codes along the way. The offers themselves may or may not be the highest available, but they are certainly the easiest.

    In a recent development, to truly optimize your returns, you'll want to compare Citi Shop earnings with those from other shopping portals — and stack other forms of saving along the way. But when that sounds like too much, the ease of this extension can still be a great way to tack on some extra returns.

    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move promptly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.
    • Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., holds a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move promptly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.

    Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.

    Sources indicate that “One of the things that we need to do is to move the Dream and Promise Act for DACA recipients and TPS recipients,” Jeffries said, referring to a Democratic bill introduced last year. “We should actually move that bill immediately.”.

    The proposal aims to create a path to citizenship for certain Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients and Temporary Protected Status holders. Similar legislation has been a top priority for Democrats in both chambers for more than a decade, with Democrats unable to advance this bill in the House while Republicans have held the majority.

    Jeffries also reiterated his calls to rein in Immigration and Customs Enforcement and redirect funding allocated to the agency through Republicans' budget law known as the One Substantial Beautiful Bill Act, while expressing a desire for bipartisan cooperation on immigration more broadly.

    According to recent reports, “We think the border should be safe and strong and secure, and we think our immigration system overall is broken,” Jeffries said. “We need to fix it in a comprehensive way, and certainly, it's our hope that a handful of Republicans will be willing to join us, so we can fix it in a bipartisan way.”.

    Industry observers note that on healthcare, however, Jeffries offered fewer specifics, suggesting Democrats still have decisions to make before taking control of the chamber. Democrats broadly agree on the need to restore subsidies for plans purchased through health insurance markets that expired at the end of 2025. But the question of what additional steps the party should pursue with the goal of expanding coverage and lowering prices is likely to be a major test of Democratic leadership’s ability to find consensus among its robust new majority.

    When asked how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that's all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    The Latest York Democrat outlined several broader healthcare priorities, including reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under President Donald Trump, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits, all of which Democrats have vowed to do over the last year.

    “Out of the gate, what we clearly have to do is fix our broken healthcare system in terms of the damage that's been done by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists over the last two years, and that clearly involves reversing the Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits, and beginning to engage in supporting medical research, particularly things like research for pediatric cancer,” Jeffries added.

    Recent findings suggest that democrats established a healthcare working group earlier this Congress, led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. and Terri Sewell, D-Ala., to gather perspectives and develop policy proposals as the party works toward a broader agenda.

    In a recent development, without an announced challenger, Jeffries has expressed confidence that he’ll secure the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who have noted they remain “undecided” ahead of Wednesday’s elections. Jeffries, who was introduced as “Speaker Jeffries” on election night, said last week he was “very confident we’ll get there” and confirmed that the caucus will hold a recorded vote in the contest.

    Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to go forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives, many aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America, had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    Jeffries said Tuesday the approach mirrors the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who is best positioned to lead based on “track record, experience and vision.”.

    It has been revealed that this report was corrected to reflect Rep. Nancy Pelosi’s status as a current member.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”.

    “When you vote, remember a party that hates America cannot be allowed to rule over the people who built our country,” Trump stated, referring to Democrats, whom he said want to “blow all of this up by electing communist jihadists.”.

    “If the people that voted for me and voted in the last election where we had such a great victory, if they go out and vote, just a good portion of them, we will win in a landslide,” Trump said midway in his speech. “Now that doesn’t happen because usually whoever the sitting president is, Republican or Democrat, uh, good or bad, good president, great president, bad, for some reason the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms, but we gave this a very strong shot.”.

    The last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the Upcoming York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the Newly introduced York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how substantial a role early votes will play in the outcome.

    • The upcoming Democratic Congress will presumably pursue policies that are advertised as ways to reduce the cost of living.
    • Joshua Bandoch is a research fellow with the Competitive Enterprise Institute, a free-market public-policy organization based in Washington, D.C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats seized control of Congress, in part by focusing on affordability and the economy. An AP-NORC survey conducted just before the election found that both were ranked top issues for registered voters, outpacing the next most key problem, health care, by about 15 percentage points.

    The upcoming Democratic Congress will presumably pursue policies that are advertised as ways to reduce the cost of living. One idea they should reject is universal basic income (UBI). Leftists have long pushed for UBI, and the idea is gaining stream among tech leaders. It’s a policy that would backfire by reigniting inflation and ultimately harming those it attempts to help.

    Joshua Bandoch is a research fellow with the Competitive Enterprise Institute, a free-market public-policy organization based in Washington, D.C.

    Kevin Corinth is the Daniel C. Searle Chair and a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.

    On “UBI Breeds Dependence and Restricts Opportunity”.

    • Industry observers note that TAP Air Portugal will launch a newly introduced thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027.
    • According to recent reports, TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the upcoming IAD-OPO route.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Washingtonians have a fresh option to Portugal next summer.

    Industry observers note that TAP Air Portugal will launch a newly introduced thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027. Westbound flights will operate on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays through the summer, and on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays beginning in October.

    According to recent reports, TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the upcoming IAD-OPO route. The long-range, single-aisle aircraft is fitted with 16 lie-flat business-class seats and 155 economy seats.

    In a recent development, the new Portugal route is the latest international addition at IAD. United intends to launch new service to Toulouse, France, in April and to Milan in May, using its new long-range A321XLR on the former route.

    International seats from IAD will increase nearly 7% in the first six months of 2027 compared to this year, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium reveals.

    IAD is undergoing a massive, $22 billion redevelopment to bring its infrastructure up to modern standards. The first piece — a 14-gate section of the latest Concourse E that includes a new, large United Club — opened earlier in November. Future phases include a new international arrivals facility that would support additional long-haul growth.

    This content is hosted by Instagram.

    And if the redevelopment proposal stays on schedule, IAD could retire its jet-age mobile lounges by the mid-2030s.

    TAP’s new OPO route complements its existing service to IAD from Lisbon Airport (LIS).

    The state-owned Portuguese airline is in the process of being privatized as part of the Lufthansa Group. The German airline conglomerate prepares to buy an initial 44.9% stake in TAP, aiming to close the deal by the first quarter of 2028.

    Lufthansa Group chief commercial officer Dieter Vranckx said in October that once the TAP deal is done, Lufthansa intends to integrate the Portuguese airline into its transatlantic joint venture with Air Canada and United.

    • Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday.
    • Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.
    • Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

    Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.

    Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.

    In a recent development, the Senate Judiciary Committee’s panel on Crime and Counterterrorism held the hearing after its Chairman Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and ranking member Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., introduced a bill Monday that would ban pre-dispute arbitration agreements from affecting cases where a minor was harmed online, including by sexual exploitation.

    It has been revealed that hawley and Durbin also worked together on a separate bill to expand eligibility for victims of abuse to bring civil suits against online platforms that intentionally, knowingly or recklessly promoted or facilitated the abuse. It would also include penalties for certain platforms that fail to report child pornography violations on their sites.

    That bill is included in a manager’s amendment to the Senate’s fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill. Durbin encouraged Congress to pass the NDAA “in the closing days” of the session because “protecting children is an crucial part of it.”.

    Sources indicate that “I have a few weeks left in my service in the United States Senate,” said Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January. “I’m thinking each day it’s coming to an end, but I want it to come [to an] end the right way.”.

    The subcommittee has spent much of the 119th Congress focused on harms to children online, including from artificial intelligence chatbots.

    Tuesday’s hearing included testimony from survivors and experts on child exploitation on Roblox.

    Hawley mentioned that victims are bound by pre-dispute agreements with Roblox to settle claims through private arbitration, rather than in court.

    It has been revealed that “They slam the courthouse door shut in their faces,” Hawley said. “We’re talking about children now, child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very tech giant that has exposed them to the content to begin with.”.

    A spokesperson for Roblox said in a statement that “safety has been central” to the platform since its launch.

    Industry observers note that “We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” the spokesperson mentioned. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a firm’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”.

    In a recent development, myriam Gilles, a professor of law at Northwestern University, told the panel that a 2022 law that ended forced arbitration agreements for victims of sexual assault has gaps. She noted Roblox has argued it does not apply to online actions, just “completed physical assault” and does not apply to platforms.

    She also said that Hawley’s fresh arbitration bill would enhance the effects of his measure regarding civil suits by making sure those suits can be heard publicly if families so choose.

    “Congress can pass laws, but if [suits] just get shunted into private arbitration, they’re doing no good in the world,” Gilles mentioned. “A right to sue that ends in secret arbitration is a right in name only.”.

    The hearing came the same day that advocates, including reality TV personality and activist Paris Hilton, held a press conference to urge House action on a bill (S 1837) that would allow individuals to bring civil suits over nonconsensual intimate depictions generated by artificial intelligence or for possession or production of deepfake porn if there was also intent to disclose the images.

    That bill passed the Senate in January but has not been taken up in the House.

    #19358. Latest Update: Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

    📅 16 Jul 2018 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1868 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Salon ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

    📅 16 Jul 2018 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Salon

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses.
    • Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.
    • Back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses. “Who Is America?” The answer, on its face, will not surprise you: we are a nation of easy marks. Not merely easy, but willing.

    Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.

    Back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom. But today, being on camera is so natural and desirable to most of us that we are willing to say or do just about anything for a few of the 15 minutes we believe to be our birthright.

    “Ali G” and the characters the show introduced, including Borat Sagdiyev and Brüno Gehard, also were born years before Project Veritas and InfoWars and other right-wing vehicles of disinformation made hidden camera hoaxing into something sinister.

    All of which is to say, “Who Is America?” is not, as Showtime would like you to believe, “the most dangerous show in history.” At best, it is an occasionally funny one.

    But to anyone who mourns the collective deterioration of our population’s capacity to engage in critical thought, but has no idea of how urgent of a crisis that happens to be, Baron Cohen’s latest endeavor is less of a comedy than a fright show. “Who Is America?” A nation of pliable dullards ripe for the hacking.

    In a recent development, “Who Is America?” was produced in secret, and its pre-show marketing largely consisted of publicized declarations of outrage by such right-wing figures as Joe Walsh, Sarah Palin and Roy Moore. Each attempted to transform their extreme embarrassment at having been duped by a British clown hiding behind layers of latex and spirit gum into some approximation of righteous anger at stated comedian’s dishonesty.

    Sources indicate that showtime, meanwhile, maintained the aura of mystery surrounding the series almost to the brink of its debut, revealing the title only a little more than a week prior. The network released the briefest of clips featuring one famous interview subject, Dick Cheney.

    This in itself was a bit of flimflam Showtime’s part: “Hope you’ll tune in next week for an interview with me,” Cheney indicates in the video, only to be a no-show in the premiere.

    You can’t blame “Who Is America?” for saving its biggest fish for later, because the famous politicians in the opener prove the problem of our collective gullibility just fine by themselves. In fact, although liberals may have gotten a hearty guffaw out of hearing Palin’s wailing about having been faked out by Baron Cohen, the very same character — Dr. Billy Wayne Ruddick Jr. PhD of Truthbrary.org — sat down for a conversation with none other than the honorable junior senator from Vermont, Bernie Sanders.

    According to recent reports, prior to the premiere Billy Wayne tweeted a response to Palin’s accusation that he made fun disabled veterans. “I did NOT say I was a War Vet,” Ruddick’s “official” response reads, going on to explain that the service was in was “not military, but United Parcel”.

    Nor does he make such assertions to Sanders, with whom he debates the merits of a universal healthcare plan. And when I say debate, what I mean is that Sanders very calmly shares statistics with Billy Wayne long after the interviewer’s line of questioning stops making sense. And when Sanders asks Billy Wayne to confirm that he is disabled, given that he is conducting the interview while seated on a motorized scooter, Baron Cohen’s character replies that no, he is not. “This here scooter is to preserve my body’s finite energy,” Billy Wayne states.

    READ MORE: That viral “strangers on a plane” Twitter story: Not a rom-com but a horror show.

    One may be tempted to qualify Sanders’ appearance by pointing out that he acquitted himself well in the face of a person best be described as a few coconuts short of a beach vacation in Binomo.

    Industry observers note that but this fails to answer the question of why Sanders signed a release, allowing this interview to be broadcast. Did anyone on Sanders’ team vet Truthbrary.org the moment Billy Wayne mentioned it? Even if they thought he was genuine, what is to be gained from being seen in a televised debate with a guy whose site includes a page titled  “Obamanoids — For Real!”?

    (To be fair, reportedly Baron Cohen almost fooled veteran news anchor Ted Koppel as part of his project. Koppel told The Hollywood Reporter that he was contacted to appear in a Showtime project titled “Age of Reason,” said to feature “conversations with distinguished experts in science and public policy, highlighting the brightest and most reputable minds on today’s most notable topics.” Koppel, perhaps receiving brainwaves from his colleague Sam Donaldson, wised up before Baron Cohen could pull him too deeply into his game.).

    It has been revealed that A second character introduced in the premiere, an NPR shirt-wearing hyper-liberal named  Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, visits the opulent South Carolina home of wealthy Trump supporters he says are  “afflicted with white privilege.” But it soon becomes clear that his marks’ problem isn’t close-mindedness but over-correcting in the acceptance department. When Baron Cohen’s interviewer waxes on about encouraging his daughter Malala to “free bleed” on the American flag as a lesson, they simply nod and listen; when he chats about his wife’s ongoing affair with a dolphin, they don’t have any questions like, say, whether what they’re hearing is real.

    This brings us to another answer to “Who Is America?”: we’re so aware of cameras, and desperate to have its focus upon us, that we will do and say anything without thinking of its possible permanence.

    Demonstrating this is Baron Cohen’s third character Rick Sherman, an ex-con turned TV host who visits a Laguna Beach, California gallery to show his work, which is a series of capable but otherwise unextraordinary portraits rendered in feces and ejaculate.

    It has been revealed that now, it’s entirely possible that the woman who runs the gallery might have been thinking she could have the next Andres Serrano on her hands. On the other hand, please.

    This is a subject entirely aware of being on view, so obsessed with appearing erudite that while Rick is off camera, having excused himself to the facilities to commit another brown-and-white vision to paper, she addresses the camera like the host she was born to be.

    “Who knew the world was capable of such oxymoronic paradoxical juxtapositions?” she muses. And this is before the homemade pubic hair paintbrush comes out.

    It has been revealed that baron Cohen has pushed the limits of tolerant everyday people many times in the past, mostly in a way that makes them look reasonable or, at the very least, more intelligent than the put-ons he inflicts upon them. And this is perhaps one of the most depressing aspects about “Who Is America?”, its demonstration of how endemic our lack of analysis truly is. I’m not saying that gallery owner is a stupid woman, understand.

    Industry observers note that but her interview is an example of prizing exposure over lasting consequence. By that I’m not merely referring to the fact that she placated a man who not only handed her pieces of cardboard purportedly smeared with his own dried excrement, or waited to receive a fresh sample of his work, but that she decided she needed to share her expert observation as to why she needed to do so by uttering a sentence full of five dollar words that add up to absolute nonsense.

    (Either that or she’s a friend of Baron Cohen’s and in on the gag. I hope it’s option two, as opposed to her actually legitimizing the artistic relevance of number two.).

    A number of reviews of “Who Is America?” have pointed out that Baron Cohen’s sneaky deceit is no longer funny because the formerly insane viewpoints Baron Cohen’s tactics expose have been normalized.

    According to recent reports, this has always been the danger, but it’s one every sort of parody or satire contends with in the current climate. It’s difficult to lampoon leaders seeking to legislate ludicrous patches to crises like gun violence instead of adopting common sense solutions like stricter regulation.

    Which brings us to the portion of “Who Is America?” guaranteed to dominate Monday’s gallery of crazy clips, fronted by Baron Cohen’s Col. Erran Morad, a self-styled Israeli anti-terrorism expert who calls himself “the terrorist terminator.”.

    The fake Mossad officer is there to promote his “Kinderguardians” program, a proposal that aims to train and arm toddlers in the classroom because, Moran notes, arming teachers is crazy.

    It has been revealed that and this is the portion that has Walsh’s boxers in a bunch, because he joins House representatives Dana Rohrabacher and Joe Wilson in lending on-camera endorsements. Walsh’s comments are interwoven with a series of fake testimonials from the likes of Larry Pratt, executive director emeritus of the lobbying group Gun Owners of America and rape joke enthusiast.

    According to recent reports, nobody forced Walsh to say, with gusto, “The way to stop a bad guy with is a good child with a gun. Happy shooting, kids!” If he didn’t want to say it, he wouldn’t have.

    What Walsh might be upset about is being upstaged by Pratt, who earns some of the episode’s biggest laughs by reading the “science” behind the effectiveness of the fake program, revealing he doesn’t know the difference between human anatomy and hitmakers who grace Billboard’s pop charts.

    Yes, “Who Is America?” gets mileage out of highlighting the callousness, sexism and extraordinary gullibility of conservatives, as Baron Cohen always has. But the things they say to him in disguise aren’t all that different than what they’d say on CNN, Fox, MSNBC or talk radio. Whatever power his comedy used to reveal is diminished by the fact that the charlatans no longer operate in secret.

    Next week’s episode introduces one or two new characters, although I don’t imagine they do anything more “dangerous” than the four we met on Sunday. For a number of viewers who love Baron Cohen’s schtick, that won’t matter.

    To them “Who Is America?” is precisely on brand, showing Americans famous and everyday reacting to bizarre situations with varying degrees of what we consider to be normalcy in a time where the baseline version of normal is constantly morphing and shifting.

    Sources indicate that to other viewers, however, “Who Is America?” is a confirmation that Baron Cohen has run some tests and can confirm there is limited and ever decreasing brain activity in this worsening patient we know as America. It is something to behold, that’s for sure. But I’m not sure it’s the stuff of groundbreaking comedy. It’s not even really news.

    #19357. Breaking: Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1000 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday.
    • Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.
    • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

    Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.

    The original ask contained roughly $12 billion that was tied directly to air traffic control upgrades, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said, with the remainder going toward long-sought airport terminal and other upgrades to aging aviation facilities.

    Duffy and Vought laid out in a letter to House and Senate appropriators on Tuesday what the extra $20 billion would be for — half for construction of five latest air route traffic control centers, and half for construction, replacement and improvement of up to 140 air traffic control towers.

    They justified the increased demand because of the “urgent need” that became evident after the ground stop. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford fanned out across the Capitol to try to sell the request, including a stop at Senate Republicans’ weekly policy lunch.

    But it quickly became evident that their own allies on Capitol Hill want more and better justification for why so much extra money is needed.

    Not only are there concerns that much of the request would go to terminal reconstruction and other longer-term projects, but lawmakers keep noting the FAA hasn’t yet spent about $8 billion out of the initial $12.5 billion “down payment” on air traffic control modernization provided in last year’s budget reconciliation law.

    “I don’t think the full $50 billion will be funded,” Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, noted Tuesday. “What we just discussed there, and what I expressed, is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.”.

    Still, Cruz mentioned the administration had done a “good job” with the initial $12.5 billion modernization proposal so far and he expected to see continued bipartisan support for the effort.

    Senate Republicans are considering adding additional aviation funds through a filibuster-proof reconciliation bill, a process that could begin as soon as this week with a floor “vote-a-rama” on a resolution to unlock that process. Cruz noted that while reconciliation could be the vehicle used, additional aviation funds need to be “safety-focused.”.

    In a recent development, sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said after the lunch with Duffy and Bedford that he expects Congress will look at a package more in the $10 billion to $30 billion range.

    For his part, Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., said the airline industry itself should foot at least a portion of the bill, considering how much federal support the carriers have received over the years.

    It has been revealed that “I don't understand why the airline industry doesn't pay for it. We give them unbelievable amounts of money,” Scott said, adding that he doesn’t like adding to the deficit and is “not major on government running things.”.

    Duffy explained the need for the high price tag as the result of decades of pent-up demand that are now threatening major disruptions and safety risks to the traveling public.

    Industry observers note that “This has never been done. To be clear, we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment that’s been a problem for decades,” he said. “I and the president have decided we are going to lean in and fix it.”.

    He called the effort a “historic investment” reflecting the ways air travel has changed since much of the nation’s infrastructure was built — noting that the newest tower was constructed in 1969 and much of the software being used is from the 1990s. Still, Duffy said, on the current course of funding, it would take 300 years to replace every U.S. tower.

    According to recent reports, “I'm not going to tell [Congress] how to do their work, but I'm telling everybody what we need,” Duffy mentioned. “And whether it's a party-line vote or if it's a bipartisan vote, I do think this is one moment in a very charged political environment — one moment where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in to do this.”.

    Even as Duffy petitioned for additional funds Tuesday, he said that the “root cause” of the equipment instability that made the ground stop necessary is still unclear as investigators analyze the router that caused the problem.

    A “routine switchover” from old copper wires to digital fiber in the telecommunications system “started to create challenges in our network,” Duffy explained Tuesday.

    The telecommunications transition includes the conversion of thousands of routers to what are known as Juniper devices — a process being undertaken by contractor L3Harris Technologies. Duffy and Bedford explained that 68 other routers had been converted without incident prior to the problematic switchover Friday.

    Bedford said Tuesday that use of the router that officials have identified as the source of the system instability has been suspended “and we've disabled the ones that are out there.”.

    The decision to suspend use of the router followed an inquiry sent to the agency by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats a day prior. “With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding safety and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” they wrote.

    Bedford remarked he was “highly confident” that similar problems wouldn’t erupt again. “Every element of this is going to be analyzed to see what we learn here and make sure that it doesn't get repeated,” he said.

    David Jordan, Lia Chien and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    📅 23 Oct 2020 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1935 w)

    Latest Update: “Borat 2” makes an America slathered in misogyny and disinformation reckon with itself

    📅 23 Oct 2020 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Salon

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On Wednesday multiple news outlets revealed the purported headliner of “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” to be none other than Rudy Giuliani, President Donald Trump’s trusted lawyer and cable news’s favorite nutcase.
    • Compared with the mock attempted kidnapping Pamela Anderson, Borat’s ultimate get in 2006’s “Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan,” the pranking of America’s mayor does not make for a grand climax or even an affectionate one.
    • In a recent development, all it took for the producers of “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” to succeed in their mission was a simple honeytrap, presented in the form of Baron Cohen’s exceptional co-star Maria Bakalova dressed as a right-wing fake news Barbie.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On Wednesday multiple news outlets revealed the purported headliner of “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” to be none other than Rudy Giuliani, President Donald Trump’s trusted lawyer and cable news’s favorite nutcase.

    Compared with the mock attempted kidnapping Pamela Anderson, Borat’s ultimate get in 2006’s “Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan,” the pranking of America’s mayor does not make for a grand climax or even an affectionate one. Instead, it more or less confirms what we already know about Rudy Giuliani: his corruptibility makes him shockingly easy to dupe.

    In a recent development, all it took for the producers of “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” to succeed in their mission was a simple honeytrap, presented in the form of Baron Cohen’s exceptional co-star Maria Bakalova dressed as a right-wing fake news Barbie. By the time we get to that scene the Bulgarian actor has solidly established that she is the reason this feminist-themed sequel works as well as it does.

    Performance-wise, Bakalova fully commits and never breaks, keeping pace with Baron Cohen in every shared sequence and commanding every scene she pilots solo. If Baron Cohen were to ever greenlight an inheritor to his Borat franchise, she would more than do it justice.

    And this illustrates the subtextual call to action throughout “Subsequent Movefilm” for women of good conscience to reclaim their power, not only at the polls but in the realm of social equity. Baron Cohen and his writers cloak this in slapstick from the moment we’re introduced to Bakalova’s Tutar, the 15-year-old daughter Borat never realized he had.

    Tutar is filthy and coarse, raised in a pen and guided by a book given to her by the Kazakh government that insists that women cannot drive, own businesses or even touch their privates without causing great disaster on par with the sinking of the Titanic. Her highest aspiration is to live in a golden cage like Queen Melania, “the happiest wife in the world,” emboldening her to join Borat’s latest trip as a stowaway.

    Similarly life, and Borat’s government, have not been kind to him since “Cultural Learnings” conquered America with great success – high five! – 14 years ago.

    In a recent development, america may have loved Borat but his countrymen, neighbors and family in his home village of Kuzcek felt great shame at how his documentary portrayed them (a nod, perhaps, at the Romanian villagers angered at being misrepresented in the 2006 film, who unsuccessfully sued its producers). In reaction he was sentenced to a life of hard labor in a gulag.

    According to recent reports, when Kazakhstan’s current Premier Nazarbayev (Dani Popescu) realizes the regime has a use for Borat, he’s hauled out of prison, shaved into a familiar form – ill-fitting grey suit, walrus mustache, puffy hairstyle and all – and given a new mission to smooth glorious leader’s entry into the world’s strongman club. How? By presenting to”Vice Premier Mikhail Pence” valuable offering: Johnny the Monkey, “Kazakhstan’s Minister of Culture and No.1 porno star.”.

    It has been revealed that this is why the Giuliani spoiler leaking before the film’s release fails to ruin “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” because, like old Johnny would do in a room full of bananas,  plunking Giuliani into a situation like the one confirmed in the film’s full title: “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm: Delivery of Prodigious Bribe to American Regime for Make Benefit Once Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan” merely yields the expected results. Giuliani was hoodwinked not by a monkey but old-fashioned monkey business. Wa-wa-wee-wa!

    In the main, the humor driving “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” is a continuation of what Baron Cohen does in his 2018 Showtime series “Who Is America?” – which is to say that he functions more as a prodding force these days than a hard crowbar. Long ago the Borat character functioned as a truth serum, the kind of amiable ignoramus people were inclined to countenance or forgive either out of politeness or a sense of superiority. Bigots would meet his bigotry with their own, perhaps, in a gesture of finding common ground, while others put up with him out of kindness.

    Now, as father and daughter embark travel through the good old U.S. of A, 2020 edition, they encounter a place where the rampant racism, anti-Semitism and Islamophobia Borat unearthed in 2006 is now on proud display across the land and slathered in misogyny.

    According to recent reports, the sexism, though, is the road by which Borat and Tutar find their way into the psyche of the ugly American – enabling them to infiltrate a debutante ball where Borat gets a father to admit he’d pay $500 for Tutar within earshot of his own child, and another man, hopelessly drunk, slurs out unbidden that men love pretty girls in South. “They’re fun!”.

    Sources indicate that following a span of time in which Borat keeps Tutar in a cage while he sleeps in the relative luxury of a horse trailer he drags behind a jalopy, “Subsequent Moviefilm” makes Tutar’s empowerment the centerpiece of the movie’s second half. Baron Cohen’s signature obviousness and a style reminiscent of director Jason Woliner’s past TV work (which includes series such as “Nathan for You”) shapes how this transpires, and the audience either accepts this for what it is or may cringe at its clunkiness.

    Either way, the fact that “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm” and Baron Cohen need Bakalova is indisputable.

    There’s the practical matter that the character of Borat is famous, for one. Back in 2007 Baron Cohen announced that he was retiring two of his alter egos, Borat and Ali G, acknowledging to The Daily Telegraph that “the problem with success, although it’s fantastic, is that every new person who sees the Borat movie is one less person I ‘get’ with Borat again, so it’s a kind of self-defeating form, really.”.

    Industry observers note that what he could not have predicted back then was how thoroughly the fabric of reality would be torn by the disinformation flood plaguing us today. However, he’s right about the problem of Borat’s fame. “Subsequent Moviefilm” confronts this early in the film when Borat sets down in America once again, only to be instantly recognized and pursued by crowds of thrilled Texans. This necessitates a trip to a local costume shop to purchase prosthetics and disguises.

    It has been revealed that nonetheless, Borat’s relevance in 2020 is debatable. Since the anti-Semitism and sexism at his heart are defining traits in a nation seized by white nationalism, that either makes him redundant or highly relevant — except for when he revealshis subjects’ prejudices.

    But then, the laugh-until-you-cry parts of the original “Borat” don’t involve, say, the Islamophobic, homophobic rodeo organizer mouthing off or those Southern frat boys wishing aloud that slavery was still legal. The best antics involve Borat’s stupidity crashing against the patience and politeness of typical Americans, or ludicrous moments like the nude wrestling match between him and his producer Azamat (Ken Davilian) that spills out of their hotel room and well into public spaces.

    Fewer of those sight gags exist in “Subsequent Moviefilm.” Save for an extended segment in which he quarantines with a pair of right-wing QAnon adherents, they have been replaced instead by situational humor, such as when Tutar swallows a plastic baby cake decoration and Borat rushes her to what he believes to be a doctor’s office. Naturally they land in crisis pregnancy center where father and daughter are counseled, not by a doctor but by Pastor Jonathan Bright. This evolves precisely as one expects it would.

    According to recent reports, then there are the bits that have already made the news: Baron Cohen’s infiltrating the Conservative Political Action Conference in February dressed as Trump? They work their way to that, and a scene from a right-wing militia gathering in Washington state where Borat performed as Country Steve and got the audience to sing along to a racist ditty, starting with lyrics about injecting Obama “with the Wuhan flu.”.

    Gotcha moments like this and the Giuliani business don’t tell us anything we don’t already know. Instead, it’s what the context implies about America’s psychological state. The cringe comedy in the crisis center isn’t merely in the pastor’s misunderstanding about the nature of the baby inside Tutar’s stomach. It is his calm insistence in her keeping it there even after Tutar’s father tells him that he put it there. (He bought the cupcake, OK?).

    But this is part of an escalating series of moments that show us who America is: a nation of very fine people who live and let prejudice flourish so long as it doesn’t disturb the status quo.

    Industry observers note that there’s the Texas baker who uses icing to pipe the words “Jews Will Not Replace Us” on a chocolate cake without batting an eyelash. There’s the shop owner who guffaws along with Borat when he asks that Tutar be directed to the “no means yes” dress section. There’s the spray tanning salon technician who, in response to Borat asking, “What color is best for racist family?” says without pause or reaction, “I wouldn’t go any darker than a six or a seven.”.

    All of these are women, by the way.

    This leads up to savior in this narrative: Jeanise Jones, a Black woman Borat hires to look after Tutar and who ends up talking some sense in to her, starting with waking her up to the fact that her father has been lying to her. (And how.) Jones is the level-headed figure in a vast land of fools; she’s also playing to the trope of the Black woman savior utilized in the first “Borat” and touted in this election cycle. Placed in the context of everyone else Borat and Tutar encounter, though, she’s a cool clarifying drink in a desert of dumb and therefore welcome.

    Evaluating the comedy value of “Subsequent Moviefilm” relative to the first “Borat” sets it up to lose, sad to say. It is enormously entertaining and, for the reasons listed above, a healthy treatment to whatever anxieties may be plaguing us a little more than a week leading up to the election. Whatever faults it has aren’t deadly, although it’s plain to see that the pandemic may have shifted the film’s ending in ways that don’t feel fully baked.

    The most prominent difference between the “Borat” of 2006 and the 2020 “Subsequent Moviefilm” is in who America is now. Our inability to agree on basic facts has only worsened since Trump’s election in 2016, to say nothing of how decline and fall of basic critical thought has left us vulnerable to benevolent pranksters like Baron Cohen and outside forces who would mean us harm.

    At the same time, there’s simply no getting around the fact that Kazakhstan receives little in the way of an image acquittal in this follow-up, an unavoidable and miserable result of alloying a problematic character to a place. If there’s a salvageable component to this, it is in how differently the sequel leaves us. When we first met Borat we comforted ourselves with the first-world notion that somehow we are better than people of so-called “lesser” nations.

    Now it doesn’t allow the audience to be so sure of itself, implying in the final scene that we aren’t merely ugly Americans. We’re a once glorious nation being led by goons who are sliding us backward into diminishment, and dangerously so. That is nothing to laugh about.

    “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm: Delivery of Prodigious Bribe to American Regime for Make Benefit Once Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan” is at the moment streaming on Amazon.

    📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2364 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Salon ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: “Chaos” in the air: Five ways voting could be disrupted on Election Day

    📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Salon

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Americans head to the polls on Tuesday, voting experts are watching to see how the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to assert more federal control over elections will play out.
    • Sources indicate that since President Donald Trump retook the White House, his administration has tried to force states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls and to restrict mail-in voting.
    • The president has justified these steps by claiming, without evidence, that American elections are beset by fraud and that illegal voting is tipping the scales in favor of Democrats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This article originally appeared on ProPublica.

    As Americans head to the polls on Tuesday, voting experts are watching to see how the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to assert more federal control over elections will play out.

    Sources indicate that since President Donald Trump retook the White House, his administration has tried to force states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls and to restrict mail-in voting. The Department of Homeland Security has used its resources to identify and prosecute noncitizen voters, an effort that has unfolded alongside the agency’s massive crackdown on immigrants.

    The president has justified these steps by claiming, without evidence, that American elections are beset by fraud and that illegal voting is tipping the scales in favor of Democrats.

    It has been revealed that courts have thwarted most of the administration’s aims to date, but Trump and his top deputies have kept up the pressure. Most recently, they’ve threatened to prosecute election officials who don’t reject ballots from people that the federal government has identified as likely noncitizens.

    The administration hasn’t explicitly ruled out sending federal agents to the polls or seizing ballots or voting machines.

    Election experts say the cumulative effect has been to ramp up anxiety about the midterms and to erode voters’ trust in the system.

    It has been revealed that “The administration has been creating a lot of noise, a lot of confusion, a lot of doubt,” said Ben Hovland, whom Trump fired as a commissioner for the bipartisan Election Assistance Commission earlier this year. He said he worries that this will make voters “sit it out” and “throw their hands up.”.

    In an emailed response to questions, a DHS spokesperson said Immigration and Customs Enforcement “is not planning operations targeting polling locations,” adding that the agency would only arrest people at the polls to address a safety threat as part of “intelligence-driven targeted enforcement.”.

    The DHS and the Justice Department “are laser focused on identifying, prosecuting and removing aliens who vote and dilute the votes of U.S. citizens,” the spokesperson added. “Our message to aliens who vote in American elections is clear: we will find you, arrest you, and you will face the consequences — including criminal charges and deportation.”.

    Before and on Election Day, it’s typical for the major political parties to mount poll-watching operations, but both Democrats and Republicans say they’ve expanded these activities in this pressurized midterm.

    Industry observers note that republicans will focus on issues such as voter eligibility and voter-roll accuracy, according to Ally Triolo, the Republican National Committee’s election integrity communications director. Democrats will concentrate on voter intimidation and other hurdles to voting, Angelo Fernández Hernández, a Democratic National Committee spokesperson, mentioned.

    Here are five concerns that voting rights experts say they’re watching as this year’s election unfolds:.

    An incident in Leon County, in the Florida Panhandle, illustrates the widespread anxiety about law enforcement at the polls.

    According to recent reports, mark Earley, the county’s supervisor of elections, told ProPublica he was “furious” when two marked U.S. Customs and Border Protection vehicles parked outside the county’s busiest early voting location last month, after he’d been repeatedly reassured by the administration that agents would not do this.

    Sources indicate that he reported the sighting to the FBI, then learned that the agents, who were headed out of state, had just stopped by to try to vote themselves. The episode generated a flurry of news coverage.

    “Given the negative media coverage regarding federal agents at the polls, it demonstrates pretty bad judgment that they showed up in their official vehicles,” Earley mentioned.

    It’s against the law for federal law enforcement to be near polling places.

    Sources indicate that nick Brown, Washington’s attorney general, leads a group of Democratic state officials and voting rights advocates who have been planning how to respond if, indeed, there is real federal interference. The group has “war-gamed” how to react if government agents attempt to commandeer voting equipment or ballots.

    In a recent development, “We’ve seen the tension and chaos that’s in the air,” Brown noted. He called the federal government “the biggest challenge to smooth elections right now, which is not the way it’s supposed to be.”.

    A DOJ spokesperson said “the best preparation for any election official is following federal law.”.

    It’s routine for DOJ monitors to watch over polling places, and the agency has assured states that, in the midterms, its observers will follow the law and not interfere with voting or election administration. Still, state officials remain concerned. During Wyoming’s primary election, poll workers stated they felt uneasy when DOJ monitors asked about their training and to inspect voting systems. The state’s governor criticized these actions as “a bit aggressive” and “irregular.”.

    The Trump administration’s multipronged effort targeting alleged noncitizen voters has already led to eligible voters being improperly removed from the rolls. Voting rights groups fear this will block some U.S. citizens from being able to vote when they show up on Tuesday.

    Federal officials have made clear they initiative to go after anyone they think is committing voter fraud.

    It has been revealed that on the first day of early voting in Texas, Aaron Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, posted a YouTube video announcing his intentions. “If you violate federal election law,” he warned, “I will hunt you down and prosecute you.”.

    In a recent development, this threat came days after the DOJ sued California, seeking to block the state from counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 voters it claims are “likely” noncitizens. The administration had obtained the state’s public voter rolls, which the DHS had blended with its own immigration information and third-party data.

    Industry observers note that in a court filing, California called the claim that there are 20,000 noncitizens on its voter rolls “specious.” Los Angeles County analyzed a sampling of the likely noncitizen voters that the federal government claimed were registered there. Many weren’t registered in the county or had never voted, the analysis indicated. Some said on their voter registration forms that they were born in the United States.

    Asked about the case, the DOJ told ProPublica, “Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections, and the Department has a duty to enforce it.”.

    It has been revealed that A federal judge has rejected the DOJ’s motion for an emergency order that would have barred California from counting the 20,000 voters’ ballots. (A federal appeals panel later backed that decision.) On Thursday, the administration sent grand jury subpoenas to California officials demanding records about their response to allegations of noncitizens on the state’s rolls. Late Friday, a federal judge issued a restraining order blocking the DOJ’s demands, calling them an “intimidation proposal” that would interfere with legal voting.

    Recent findings suggest that last week, the DOJ wrote a letter threatening to sue Washington state if officials there refused to review a list of 400 voters it believes to be noncitizens within 24 hours. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters late last month that the department was considering additional actions, saying there were “a number of states that we’re looking at.”.

    In a letter responding to the DOJ, Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs called the government list of 400 names “not reliable,” saying it included U.S. citizens, people who aren’t registered to vote and duplicate entries. “Time and time again,” Hobbs wrote, “DHS claims about noncitizen voter registration turn out to be greatly exaggerated or false.”.

    Sam Trepel is Rule of Law program director at States United Democracy Center and a former attorney for the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division. She noted the agency’s actions involving California and Washington were a “disturbing use of prosecutorial authority.”.

    Trepel worries that the DOJ may try to seize ballots cast by voters identified as likely noncitizens, before or after the election, which would “put their votes at risk and undermine trust more broadly.”.

    Voting rights advocates also worry that the government’s efforts to target noncitizen voters could frighten eligible voters to the point that they won’t show up.

    A federal judge recently put limits on a multistate effort by the DHS to go door-to-door in search of suspected noncitizen voters, at least through Election Day, saying it was illegally intimidating legal voters.

    “A voter could say, ‘Well, maybe I don’t want to put myself on the target list here, maybe I won’t register, or maybe I won’t vote,’” said David Janovsky, acting director of The Constitution Project at the watchdog group Project on Government Oversight.

    States often change laws and rules related to voting.

    Since 2024, Republican-led states have taken a number of steps that experts say will make it more difficult for some of their residents to cast ballots and have them count.

    In a recent development, A North Carolina law, for example, requires voters to provide proof of identification when sending mail-in ballots. Under new rules, ballots now come with two envelopes, both of which must be sealed. Ballot rejections have skyrocketed, Democracy Docket reported, because voters aren’t sealing the inner envelope.

    According to recent reports, texas and other states have cut back on the number and location of polling places, especially in areas favoring Democrats. In hotly contested Tarrant County, which includes Fort Worth, the number of polling sites was slashed by almost a third. This could increase the risk of long lines and voter confusion on Election Day.

    Voting rights groups such as the Texas Civil Rights Project are tracking two problems involving the state’s voter registration systems. A software error at the Texas Department of Public Safety stopped several hundred thousand new voter registrations from being forwarded to local election officials, preventing them from being added to the rolls. A separate state system for updating registration information wasn’t processing changes for several weeks, leading to more backlogs. Counties say they’ve been able to address these problems.

    Every election features some issues with voting equipment.

    So far, there have been isolated complaints involving touch-screen voting machines — including one from Dolly Parton’s sister in Tennessee — spawning fears that machines have been “rigged” to switch votes.

    According to recent reports, ES&S, the firm that makes the machines garnering the complaints, told ProPublica that the company hadn’t received widespread reports. Election experts say occasional problems with touch-screen machines don’t signify tampering or manipulation. Any attempt to tamper with programming would surface during testing by election officials and be corrected, they noted.

    Incidents in the run-up to the midterms have ratcheted up election officials’ concerns about the potential for both cyber and physical attacks.

    Last month, officials in several states, including Arizona, received envelopes with an unknown white powder. Arizona eventually deemed the material nontoxic, but Secretary of State Adrian Fontes said “the fear it caused was real.”.

    It has been revealed that in 2024, false bomb threats, thought to be from foreign actors, caused widespread evacuations of vote-counting sites across the country. The disruptions were brief, however, in part because a message board funded by the federal Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, or CISA, alerted election officials that the FBI had deemed the threats not credible.

    Recent findings suggest that trump, however, has dismantled CISA since retaking the presidency, leaving states and local election officials to grapple with both physical and cyber threats on their own. Election nonprofits have stepped up to try to fill the gap, and states, with CISA’s help, have enhanced their own cyber defenses.

    Derek Tisler, counsel and manager for the elections and government program at the Brennan Center for Justice, said the federal government’s absence has weakened the defenses.

    “States acting on their own just do not have the same power,” he mentioned.

    Election lawyers fear that actions by the Trump administration in the run-up to the midterms suggest the government will aggressively pursue postelection challenges if the results are not to the president’s liking.

    Recent findings suggest that late last month, the DOJ sued Alaska, seeking to block the state from certifying the result of its Senate race if the Republican incumbent doesn’t win. A federal judge threw out that lawsuit on Sunday, but the administration is expected to appeal.

    In a recent development, trump has noted he personally ordered the lawsuit to be filed. It claims the system is unfairly rigged against Sen. Dan Sullivan, because another Alaska man named Dan Sullivan also qualified for the general election ballot. The Upcoming York Times reported last week that campaign aides to Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola orchestrated the candidacy of the second Dan Sullivan after a monthslong, statewide search to recruit someone with the same name.

    Industry observers note that nonetheless, the DOJ’s case is unusual, both because federal law prohibits the government from interfering with an active election and because challenges typically come after voting is complete. Postelection challenges are most often brought by losing candidates in state courts.

    “This is using the federal government to interfere with our election process in a way that I think is pretty troubling on multiple levels,” stated Brown, the Washington attorney general.

    In response to ProPublica’s questions, the DOJ pointed to Blanche’s statement about the lawsuit on social media, which stated the agency “does not seek to stop any ballot from being cast or to stop the certification of Alaska’s election.” (The lawsuit calls it “vital” that the state not certify “any election result that may be impacted by voter confusion” and asks the judge to prevent Alaska from doing this.).

    Some election lawyers have suggested that if the GOP suffers significant losses, Trump could try to pressure Republicans in Congress to block newly introduced members from being seated. Several lawyers, including Derek Muller, a law professor at the University of Notre Dame, say that the incoming Democratic majority would be able to fend off such an effort; courts, too, are likely to stymie it, though it might cause a short delay, according to Muller.

    Brown said he and other attorneys general are also planning how to respond if local election officials or boards refuse to certify election results, based on their own claims of fraud or claims by the administration.

    “I worry tremendously about what they might do,” Brown said.
